lessons.title: What certification buys you
lessons.why: Microsoft supports Direct Routing on certified SBCs. Everything else can be refused.
body: The certified list is the support boundary. AudioCodes, Ribbon, Oracle, and Cisco CUBE are families you will meet. A logo is not a certification. The software release has to be on the list.
When it breaks, you call the vendor. They escalate to Microsoft if they must. Open that path with firmware, a ladder, and the paired FQDN. A homemade SBC with a clever config is an unsupported trunk.

chart.title: Support path
chart.note: Order of calls during an incident.

lessons.say: Certification is a release on Microsoft’s list. Support starts with the vendor.
lessons.fault: A case is opened on an unlisted SBC with no logs.
lessons.listen: Use a certified SBC release. Call the vendor first, with logs.

lessons.title: AudioCodes pattern
lessons.why: Mediant SBCs are common in Teams designs. The pattern is still the shared gate, plus their guide.
body: AudioCodes documents Direct Routing for specific Mediant releases, often with their management tools beside the SBC. Use the document that matches the firmware. A 2019 forum post is not that document.

The shared gate still applies: public certificate, verified domain, three proxies, OPTIONS, media ports, a second path, and an emergency test. Their syntax is their problem. Your job is to know which gate failed.
lessons.say: I follow AudioCodes’ current guide for the firmware, and I still check the shared gate.
lessons.fault: A forum config is pasted onto new firmware and OPTIONS never get a 200.
lessons.listen: AudioCodes is a certified family. Use their current guide, and do not skip the shared certificate and media gates.

lessons.title: Ribbon pattern
lessons.why: Ribbon Core and software editions differ. The brand is not the release.
body: Ribbon SBCs are a normal Direct Routing choice when the edition and release are certified. Answer OPTIONS on the interface Teams will actually reach. A 200 on the management port does not count.
Same support rule: Ribbon first. Bring their show-tech equivalent and a SIP ladder with the Call-ID.
lessons.say: I confirm the Ribbon release and the interface that answers OPTIONS.
lessons.fault: OPTIONS are answered on the wrong interface, so Teams marks the trunk down.
lessons.listen: For Ribbon, match the certified edition and answer OPTIONS on the signaling interface.

lessons.title: Oracle Communications SBC
lessons.why: Oracle’s session border controller is a Direct Routing option only on the releases Microsoft lists.
body: Check the certified list for the Oracle software version, not the product family name. An unlisted release is an unsupported trunk no matter how complete the configuration looks.
Certificate name, TLS version, and early offer still apply. Oracle’s configuration model is its own language. Translate the shared gate into that language using their current guide.
lessons.say: I match the Oracle release to the certified list before I praise the config.
lessons.fault: The config is one release below the list and Microsoft declines the case.
lessons.listen: Oracle SBCs count only when that release is on Microsoft’s certified list.

lessons.title: Cisco CUBE for Teams
lessons.why: CUBE is the usual bridge when CUCM is still in the building. It is still an SBC.
body: Cisco Unified Border Element on a certified IOS-XE release peers TLS with the three commercial proxies, presents a certificate whose SAN matches the paired FQDN, and has dial-peers toward Teams and toward CUCM or the carrier. Teams expects early offer. A delayed-offer trunk from CUCM pushed all the way to Teams negotiates badly.

This campus does not paste a production dial-peer. Use Cisco’s current CUBE for Teams guide for the release you run. Trust the published signaling ranges rather than a single DNS answer. Offer a codec both sides share, G.711 at minimum unless you have a measured reason not to.
lessons.say: CUBE is a certified SBC with dial-peers in two directions and early offer toward Teams.
lessons.fault: CUCM sends delayed offer all the way to Teams and calls fail with 488.
lessons.listen: Use a certified CUBE release, early offer toward Teams, and a certificate name that matches the paired FQDN.

lessons.title: The support boundary
lessons.why: Knowing who you call is part of the design.
body: Collect the firmware, the paired FQDN, a ladder with Call-ID, and the OPTIONS history before you call. The vendor investigates. Microsoft may decline a case on a non-certified SBC.
Keep a screenshot of the certified list from the week you bought. A 2022 PDF in the project folder is how you discover you are unsupported during the outage.
lessons.say: Vendor first, with firmware and a Call-ID. I keep the certified-list date.
lessons.fault: The outage call starts with no logs and an unlisted build.
lessons.listen: Open SBC tickets with the vendor, the firmware, and a Call-ID. Keep the certification evidence.
